messages:
Noah (AE): Peregrine procurement paused the POC. CFO emailed: three absolute yes/no items before exec signoff — 1) HSM-only (no key export), 2) egress via customer gateway (private peering), 3) a short pilot latency commitment. Ask: can we get owners and a bridge tomorrow?
Cam (SE): Ack. Quick clarification: HSM-only means live crypto ops on their appliance, no import?
Noah (AE): Correct. They said keys must never leave their HSM and signing calls should land on-prem.
Ivy (Presales): Reality check: we don't support direct HSM RPC peering as a standard feature. We can propose two options: A) KMS-proxy that forwards signing to their HSM over a mutual TLS tunnel (cert exchange required), or B) cloud-KMS BYOK with attestations if they allow import. Both need security + legal review.
Rashid (SRE): Ops input: target during pilot is ~650 qps, seq=64. Baseline internal perf for rw-v2-large seq64: p50=46ms, p95=125ms. Expect p95 tail increase if HSM roundtrip is in path. For pilot we recommend Dedicated pool w/ 3 nodes + warm canary and `--kv-cache` enabled.
Zara (Security): Security red flags: live HSM peering increases attack surface. Need: vendor FIPS cert, network diagram, MTLS config, threat model, and HSM attestation form filled by them. We'll also ask whether they require a specific cipher suite and whether HSM calls are synchronous blocking ops.
Owen (Legal): Legal take: HSM peering will require a crypto addendum and specific liability carve-outs. Pilot SLAs are unusual but we can offer a timeboxed operational commitment with capped credits. Send procurement redlines asap.
Marta (CS): Customer priority is key sovereignty. They prefer speed but said they won't trade away key control. We should make the HSM path explicit and show the fallback.
Cam (SE): I'll prepare a 1-page diagram: direct HSM peering vs KMS-proxy fallback, plus a short prescriptive list for their network team (ports, cert exchange steps).
Ivy (Presales): I'll draft a 3-slide bridge deck: asks, options + tradeoffs, timeline + owners. Proposed timeline: Day 0-2 contract + cert exchange, Day 3-5 MTLS + HSM smoke tests, Day 6-8 perf tuning, Day 9 exec signoff.
Rashid (SRE): Action: I'll spin a staging cluster and run a mocked-HSM smoke to surface tail latencies tomorrow AM. Command I'll use: `./smoke_test --model rw-v2-large --concurrency 650 --seq 64 --kv-cache --mock-hsm-latency=20ms`
Zara (Security): I'll pull the HSM attestation template and send to their SOC contact. Also starting a short risk note for the bridge.
Owen (Legal): I'll pre-draft a limited-scope crypto addendum and a pilot SLA (credits capped) for Sales Legal to review. Noah, pls forward any procurement language.
ops-bot: ticket #SLS-31278 created: "Peregrine POC - HSM peering + private egress + pilot SLA" assigned to eng-oncall. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SLS-31278
Noah (AE): Can we do an exec bridge tomorrow 8:45am PT? CFO prefers early slot.
Rashid (SRE): 8:45am PT works for SRE. I'll be on the bridge with early perf notes.
Cam (SE): I'll join and share the network diag and the runbook for the cert exchange.
Ivy (Presales): I'll lead the bridge and present the options + timeline.
Zara (Security): I'll join for attestation and risk summary.
Owen (Legal): I'll be on standby; will join if procurement asks for contract language.
Marta (CS): I'll coordinate the calendar and send the invite once Noah confirms.
Noah (AE): Owners: Rashid -> perf smoke & ops checklist; Cam -> network diag & runbook; Ivy -> deck + timeline; Zara -> attestation & risk note; Owen -> addendum draft; Marta -> customer comms. We need perf numbers + draft SLA before 7:30am PT to finalize slides.
Ivy (Presales): Note for bridge slides: include `--kv-cache` and `--batch-policy=aggressive` as recommended knobs. Also show fallback: cache-backed responses or smaller model if peering causes high tails.
Rashid (SRE): I'll post the smoke-run logs in this thread after the run and tag any anomalies.
Noah (AE): Thanks team. Critical: make the HSM path explicit and show the safe fallback so the CFO has options on the bridge. :white_check_mark:
